56699-the-stone-axe-of-burkamukk:
Mary Grant Bruce wrote tales for children drawn from Aboriginal story, issued in London and Melbourne in 1922 with drawings by Macfarlane. The first tale gives the book its name. Burkamukk the chief has chosen his camp well, in a green glade near a wide creek and a food-rich swamp.

His people are fat and contented, with skin rugs sewn by the women using needles of kangaroo bone. Later tales tell of Waung the crow, the emu who would dance, and Booran the pelican. Others explain how light came, why the frog laughed, and how the stars were set. Bruce retells these stories in a warm, fireside voice.

A founder of VICE speaks with Danny Jones in a heavily censored episode. The show warns that parts were cut for harsh topics and language. A full version was offered to paying members only.

The guest, now cast out from the firm he helped build, names a top villain in political media. Talk turns raw on race, fame, and old grudges. Jones lets the guest vent while testing his claims. The episode captures a media insider in exile, bitter and blunt, with a story that mainstream outlets rarely air in full.
